The '''Borg cipher''' is an [[Cipher|encrypted]] manuscript, probably from the 1600s, describing treatment of symptoms and diseases. The manuscript consists of 408 handwritten pages. The only unencrypted parts are the first page in Arabic, some fragments and headings in Latin, and the last two pages in Italian. It is stored at the [[Vatican Library]] under the name ''[https://digi.vatlib.it/view/MSS_Borg.lat.898 MSS-Borg.lat.898].<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Yin |first1=Xusen |last2=Aldarrab |first2=Nada |last3=Megyesi |first3=Beata |last4=Knight |first4=Kevin |chapter=Decipherment of Historical Manuscript Images |date=20-25 September 2019 |title=2019 International Conference on Document Analysis and Recognition (ICDAR) |chapter-url=https://doi.org/10.1109/icdar.2019.00022 |publisher=IEEE |pages=78–85 |doi=10.1109/icdar.2019.00022 |isbn=978-1-7281-3014-9 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-05-28 |title=Plots, love letters and remedies: The medieval secrets being revealed by AI |url=https://www.bbc.com/future/article/20260527-plots-love-letters-and-diplomacy-the-medieval-secrets-being-revealed-by-ai |access-date=2026-05-31 |website=www.bbc.com |language=en-GB}}</ref>''

== Cipher ==
The cipher includes 34 different characters, including graphic signs and [[Latin script|Roman letters]] with [[Diacritic|diacritics]]. It was decoded in 2016 by Nada Aldarrab, Kevin Knight and Beáta Megyesi.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Borg Cipher - Stockholms universitet |url=https://www.su.se/english/research/research-catalogue/research-projects/d/decipherment-of-historical-manuscripts/the-borg-cipher |access-date=2026-05-31 |website=www.su.se |language=en}}</ref>
